cards.definition: A merchant-to-merchant (B2B) sale of goods, as opposed to consumer retail, services, IP licences, land, or securities.
cards.example: Selling 2,000 office chairs to a foreign distributor is a commercial sale; selling one chair to a shopper is not.

zh-Hans.definition: 商人之间（B2B）的货物买卖，区别于消费零售、服务、知识产权许可、不动产或证券交易。

cards.definition: A sale where the seller must deliver both conforming goods and conforming documents; payment and control of the goods move with the paper.
cards.example: Under a documentary sale paid by L/C, a wrong bill of lading can block payment even if the goods are perfect.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方既要交付相符货物，又要提交相符单据的买卖；付款和货物控制权随单据转移。

cards.definition: International Chamber of Commerce — private business organisation that publishes Incoterms®, UCP, URC, model contracts, and runs a leading arbitration court.
cards.example: The credit says “subject to UCP 600”, an ICC publication.

zh-Hans.definition: 私营国际商业组织，制定国际贸易术语解释通则、UCP、URC、示范合同，并设有国际仲裁院。

cards.definition: World Trade Organization — intergovernmental body (since 1995, succeeding GATT) setting rules governments must follow on trade barriers and settling disputes between states.
cards.example: WTO rules limit a government’s tariffs, but they do not fill in your letter of credit.

zh-Hans.definition: 1995年继承关贸总协定的政府间组织，规定各国贸易壁垒规则并解决国家间贸易争端。

cards.definition: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (1947) — the post-war multilateral treaty that cut tariffs; its rules continue as GATT 1994 inside the WTO.
cards.example: GATT negotiating rounds cut average industrial tariffs dramatically before the WTO existed.

zh-Hans.definition: 1947年签订的多边条约，大幅降低关税；其规则以“1994年关贸总协定”形式延续于世贸组织体系中。

cards.definition: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law — drafts uniform trade-law instruments such as the CISG and the model arbitration law.
cards.example: The CISG text is published on the UNCITRAL website.

zh-Hans.term: 联合国国际贸易法委员会
zh-Hans.definition: 起草统一国际贸易法律文件（如《联合国国际货物销售合同公约》和仲裁示范法）的联合国机构。

cards.definition: Local or national business association; in trade it commonly issues certificates of origin and ATA Carnets.
cards.example: The exporter’s local chamber certifies the certificate of origin.

zh-Hans.definition: 地方或全国性商业协会；在贸易中常签发原产地证书和ATA单证册。

cards.definition: Agent that books and coordinates transport for a shipper and often prepares or collects the shipping documents.
cards.example: Tell your freight forwarder the Incoterm you sold under so the booking matches the sale.

zh-Hans.definition: 为托运人订舱、协调运输，并常代为准备或收集运输单据的代理人。

cards.definition: Licensed agent that files customs declarations and pays duties on behalf of an importer or exporter.
cards.example: Under DAP, the buyer’s customs broker clears the goods for import.

zh-Hans.definition: 代表进出口商办理海关申报并缴纳关税的持牌代理人。

cards.definition: Risk that events in the buyer’s country — war, political change, currency or payment controls — stop or delay payment or delivery.
cards.example: A confirmed L/C protects the exporter against country risk in the buyer’s market.

zh-Hans.definition: 买方所在国发生战争、政局变化、外汇或付款管制等事件，导致付款或交货受阻的风险。

cards.definition: Request for quotation — a buyer’s inquiry asking for price and terms; usually not yet a binding offer. A complex version is an RFP (request for proposal).
cards.example: The importer sends an RFQ after meeting the exporter at a trade fair.

zh-Hans.definition: 买方询问价格和条件的询盘，一般尚不构成有约束力的要约；复杂项目称为建议征求书（RFP）。

cards.definition: Advance version of the commercial invoice showing price, delivery, and payment terms; may be the seller’s binding offer and is used to open L/Cs and obtain import licences.
cards.example: The bank opens the letter of credit on the basis of the seller’s pro forma invoice.

zh-Hans.definition: 商业发票的预先版本，列明价格、交货和付款条件；可构成卖方的正式要约，并用于开立信用证和申请进口许可证。

cards.definition: The buyer’s order document; either the first binding offer (seller then confirms) or the acceptance of a seller’s pro forma.
cards.example: A large retailer’s PO usually carries its own general conditions of purchase.

zh-Hans.definition: 买方的订货单据；可能是首个有约束力的要约（由卖方确认），也可能是对卖方形式发票的承诺。

cards.definition: The seller’s acceptance of a buyer’s purchase order, concluding the contract when the PO was the offer.
cards.example: The contract was formed when the exporter sent its order confirmation.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方对买方采购订单的承诺；当采购订单为要约时，确认书使合同成立。

cards.definition: The seller’s bill for the goods: parties, description, quantities, prices, terms; other documents and the L/C are checked against it, so it must be exact.
cards.example: A model number typo on the commercial invoice made the whole presentation discrepant.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方开具的货物账单，列明当事人、品名、数量、价格及条件；其他单据和信用证均以其为核对基础，必须准确无误。

cards.definition: Document listing the contents, type, and marks of each package in a shipment.
cards.example: Customs used the packing list to find the carton holding the sample units.

zh-Hans.definition: 列明每件包装的内容、包装类型及唛头的单据。

cards.definition: Document stating the country where goods were produced; usually issued by a chamber of commerce; affects tariffs and trade preferences.
cards.example: The buyer needed a certificate of origin to claim the preferential tariff rate.

zh-Hans.definition: 证明货物生产国的单据，通常由商会签发，影响关税及贸易优惠待遇。

cards.definition: Report by an independent inspection agency on the quality or quantity of goods; often required under an L/C to protect the buyer.
cards.example: The L/C required an inspection certificate from an independent agency stating minimum protein content.

zh-Hans.definition: 独立检验机构出具的货物品质或数量报告；常作为信用证单据要求以保护买方。

cards.definition: Invoice certified by a consul of the importing country, still required by a few countries for customs purposes.
cards.example: The importing country’s consulate stamped the consular invoice before shipment.

zh-Hans.definition: 经进口国领事认证的发票，少数国家仍要求用于海关目的。

cards.definition: Carrier’s sea transport document with three functions: receipt for the goods, evidence of the carriage contract, and (if “to order”) control of the goods.
cards.example: The buyer presents the original bill of lading to the carrier to collect the cargo.

zh-Hans.definition: 承运人签发的海运单据，具有三项功能：货物收据、运输合同证明，以及（指示提单）对货物的控制权。

cards.definition: Negotiable B/L made out “to order”; transferable by endorsement, so the holder controls delivery and banks can use it as security.
cards.example: Because it was an order B/L, the cargo could be resold while still at sea.

zh-Hans.definition: 抬头为“凭指示”的可转让提单；可背书转让，持有人控制提货，银行可作为担保物。

cards.definition: Non-negotiable B/L naming a specific consignee; little security value to banks.
cards.example: With a straight B/L naming the buyer, the bank could not control the goods.

zh-Hans.definition: 载明特定收货人的不可转让提单，对银行的担保价值很低。

cards.definition: Non-negotiable transport receipt; the named consignee collects without presenting an original document. Fast, but gives banks almost no security.
cards.example: Regular shipments between affiliates moved on sea waybills to avoid waiting for original documents.

zh-Hans.definition: 不可转让的运输收据，指定收货人无需出示正本即可提货；速度快，但几乎不能为银行提供担保。

cards.definition: B/L with no notation of damage or defect in the goods or packaging — what L/Cs normally require.
cards.example: The credit called for a clean on-board bill of lading.

zh-Hans.definition: 未批注货物或包装有缺陷的提单，信用证通常要求此类提单。

cards.definition: B/L on which the carrier noted damage or a defect (e.g. “3 cartons crushed”); usually rejected under an L/C.
cards.example: A claused B/L turned a complying presentation into a discrepant one.

zh-Hans.definition: 承运人批注货物有损坏或缺陷（如“3箱压坏”）的提单；在信用证下通常被拒收。

cards.definition: Notation that goods have been loaded on the named vessel; the delivery point for FOB, CFR, and CIF.
cards.example: The credit required an “on board” notation dated no later than 30 June.

zh-Hans.definition: 表明货物已装上指定船舶的批注；是FOB、CFR和CIF的交货点。

cards.definition: ICC trade terms that allocate costs, risk, customs duties, and (for CIF/CIP) insurance between seller and buyer. Always cite rule + named place + edition.
cards.example: “USD 12 per unit FCA Rotterdam Incoterms® 2020.”

zh-Hans.term: 国际贸易术语解释通则
zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会制定的贸易术语，在买卖双方之间分配费用、风险、清关责任及（CIF/CIP下的）保险义务；须写明术语、指定地点和版本。

cards.definition: The location written after an Incoterm that fixes where delivery (or, for C-terms, paid carriage) happens.
cards.example: In “DAP Lyon warehouse 4”, the named place is the warehouse.

zh-Hans.definition: 写在贸易术语之后、确定交货地点（C组术语中为运费付至地点）的位置。

cards.definition: Ex Works — seller makes goods available at its premises; buyer loads, clears export, and bears all cost and risk from there. Minimum seller duty.
cards.example: “EXW Shenzhen factory” — the buyer’s truck collects and the buyer handles export clearance.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方在其所在地将货物交由买方处置；买方负责装货、出口清关并承担此后全部费用和风险；卖方义务最小。

cards.definition: Free Carrier — seller clears export and hands goods to the buyer’s carrier at the named place; risk passes there. Any mode; the usual choice for containers.
cards.example: “FCA Hamburg container terminal” suits containerised goods better than FOB.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方办理出口清关，在指定地点将货物交给买方指定的承运人，风险于此转移；适用于任何运输方式，集装箱货物常用。

cards.definition: Carriage Paid To — seller hands goods to the carrier and pays carriage to the named destination; risk passes at hand-over, not at destination.
cards.example: “CPT Chicago”: the seller pays freight to Chicago, but transit risk is the buyer’s.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方将货物交给承运人并支付至指定目的地的运费；风险在交给承运人时转移，而非在目的地。

cards.definition: Carriage and Insurance Paid To — CPT plus insurance bought by the seller for the buyer (Incoterms® 2020: all-risks ICC (A) cover by default).
cards.example: “CIP Nairobi airport”: the seller pays air freight and insures the cargo for 110% of value.

zh-Hans.definition: CPT加上卖方为买方投保（2020版默认须投保协会货物条款(A)一切险）。

cards.definition: Delivered at Terminal (2010), renamed Delivered at Place Unloaded (2020) — seller delivers goods unloaded at the named place.
cards.example: “DPU Antwerp terminal”: the seller pays to unload the containers.

zh-Hans.term: 运输终端交货／卸货地交货
zh-Hans.definition: 2010版为运输终端交货（DAT），2020版改为卸货地交货（DPU）：卖方在指定地点卸货后交货。

cards.definition: Delivered at Place — seller delivers at the named destination ready for unloading, not import-cleared; buyer pays import duties.
cards.example: “DAP buyer’s warehouse, Toronto”: the buyer clears customs and unloads.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方在指定目的地将货物置于买方处置之下（待卸货），不办理进口清关；进口关税由买方承担。

cards.definition: Delivered Duty Paid — seller delivers at destination, import-cleared with duties paid. Maximum seller duty; avoid if the seller cannot clear imports.
cards.example: A seller quoting DDP must be able to act as importer of record in the buyer’s country.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方在目的地交货并办理进口清关、缴纳关税；卖方义务最大，若卖方无法在进口国清关则不宜使用。

cards.definition: Free Alongside Ship — seller delivers goods alongside the vessel at the named port of shipment. Sea and inland waterway only; mainly bulk cargo.
cards.example: “FAS Santos” for a bulk sugar cargo placed on the quay beside the ship.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方在指定装运港将货物交到船边；仅适用于海运和内河运输，主要用于散货。

cards.definition: Free On Board — seller delivers once goods are on board the vessel at the named port; risk passes then. Sea and inland waterway only.
cards.example: “FOB Shanghai”: the buyer books and pays the ocean freight.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方在指定装运港将货物装上船即完成交货，风险随之转移；仅适用于海运和内河运输。

cards.definition: Cost and Freight — seller loads on board and pays freight to the named destination port; risk passes on board at shipment.
cards.example: “CFR Mombasa”: freight is paid to Mombasa, but sea risk is the buyer’s.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方装船并支付至指定目的港的运费；风险在装运港装船时转移。

cards.definition: Cost, Insurance and Freight — CFR plus minimum cargo insurance (ICC (C), 110% of price) bought by the seller for the buyer. A shipment contract.
cards.example: “CIF New York”: if the cargo sinks after loading, the buyer claims on the insurance.

zh-Hans.definition: CFR加上卖方为买方投保最低险别（协会货物条款(C)，按价格110%）；属于装运合同。

cards.definition: Sale where the seller completes delivery at the shipment or hand-over point (E, F, and C terms); transit risk is the buyer’s.
cards.example: CIF is a shipment contract even though the seller pays freight to destination.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方在装运或交付承运人时即完成交货的买卖（E、F、C组术语），运输途中风险由买方承担。

cards.definition: Sale where the seller bears risk until goods reach the named destination (D terms).
cards.example: Under a DAP arrival contract, cargo lost at sea is the seller’s problem.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方承担风险直至货物到达指定目的地的买卖（D组术语）。

cards.definition: Goods sold several times while in transit; middle sellers “procure goods shipped” instead of loading them.
cards.example: An oil cargo changed hands four times in a string sale before discharge.

zh-Hans.definition: 货物在运输途中被多次转售；中间卖方以“取得已装运货物”方式履行交货。

cards.definition: Standard London-market marine cargo cover wordings: (A) all risks, (B) intermediate, (C) minimum named perils.
cards.example: Minimum (C) cover does not protect high-value electronics against theft.

zh-Hans.definition: 伦敦市场标准海运货物保险条款：(A)一切险，(B)中等险，(C)最低险（列明风险）。

cards.definition: Carriage-contract terms on who pays loading and unloading at port — between shipper and carrier, not seller and buyer. Not the same as Incoterms®.
cards.example: Liner terms in the freight booking do not change the risk transfer under the sale’s FOB term.

zh-Hans.definition: 运输合同中关于港口装卸费用由谁承担的条款，约束托运人与承运人，而非买卖双方；不同于贸易术语。

cards.definition: UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods — uniform rules on forming and performing B2B international sales; applies automatically between contracting states unless expressly excluded.
cards.example: Writing only “governed by New York law” does not exclude the CISG.

zh-Hans.term: 联合国国际货物销售合同公约
zh-Hans.definition: 关于国际货物买卖合同订立和履行的统一规则；在缔约国之间自动适用，除非明确排除。

aliases: UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods

cards.definition: The “law merchant”: customs and principles of international trade developed by merchants across centuries, underlying the CISG and arbitral practice.
cards.example: An arbitral tribunal may decide a gap under the lex mercatoria.

zh-Hans.definition: 历经数百年由商人形成的国际贸易惯例和原则，是CISG及仲裁实践的基础。

cards.definition: Non-binding general principles of international commercial contracts that parties or arbitrators may choose as the applicable rules.
cards.example: The parties chose the UNIDROIT Principles to avoid either national law.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际统一私法协会制定的不具强制力的国际商事合同一般原则，可由当事人或仲裁员选择适用。

cards.definition: A proposal addressed to specific persons that is sufficiently definite (goods, quantity, price) and shows intent to be bound if accepted.
cards.example: A price list marked “not an offer” avoids being bound by every order.

zh-Hans.definition: 向特定人发出、内容足够确定（货物、数量、价格）并表明一经承诺即受约束的意思表示。

cards.definition: Assent to an offer; under the CISG effective when it reaches the offeror. Once dispatched, the offer can no longer be revoked.
cards.example: The contract was concluded when the emailed acceptance reached the seller.

zh-Hans.definition: 同意要约的意思表示；在CISG下于到达要约人时生效，一经发出要约即不可撤销。

cards.definition: A reply that changes material terms of an offer; it rejects the original offer and becomes a new offer.
cards.example: Changing the delivery date in the PO turned it into a counter-offer.

zh-Hans.definition: 对要约的实质性条款作出变更的答复；构成对原要约的拒绝并成为新要约。

cards.definition: Conflict when buyer and seller exchange printed forms with differing terms; under the CISG material differences create a counter-offer — try to “fire the last shot”.
cards.example: The seller’s acknowledgement form, sent last, carried its own general conditions.

zh-Hans.definition: 买卖双方交换条款不一致的格式文件所产生的冲突；CISG下实质性差异构成反要约，应争取“最后一枪”。

cards.definition: Under the CISG: price, payment, quality, quantity, place and time of delivery, liability, and dispute settlement — changing one makes a reply a counter-offer.
cards.example: A different payment term in the reply is a material change.

zh-Hans.definition: CISG下的价格、付款、质量、数量、交货地点和时间、赔偿责任及争议解决等条款；变更其一即构成反要约。

cards.definition: Legal family based on comprehensive codes (Roman law, French and German codes); judges apply the code and treat precedent as persuasive.
cards.example: France, Germany, Japan, and most of Latin America are civil-law systems.

zh-Hans.definition: 以成文法典为基础的法系（源于罗马法、法德民法典）；法官适用法典，判例仅具参考作用。

cards.definition: Legal family from English law in which courts are bound by precedent and develop law case by case.
cards.example: U.S. contracts are long partly because common law relies on freedom of contract and precedent.

zh-Hans.definition: 源于英国法的法系，法院受先例约束，通过判例逐案发展法律。

cards.definition: Islamic law, derived from religious sources and respectful of commercial custom; applied to varying degrees in many Muslim-majority states.
cards.example: Financing in a Shari’a market may use profit-sharing instead of interest.

zh-Hans.definition: 源于宗教经典、尊重商业惯例的伊斯兰法；在许多穆斯林国家不同程度地适用。

cards.definition: Shari’a doctrine often read as prohibiting interest; drives alternative Islamic finance structures.
cards.example: Because of riba, the deal used a mark-up sale instead of an interest-bearing loan.

zh-Hans.definition: 伊斯兰教法中通常被理解为禁止收取利息的原则，催生了伊斯兰金融替代结构。

cards.definition: A court’s or tribunal’s power to hear and decide a dispute.
cards.example: Without a forum clause, courts in three countries claimed jurisdiction.

zh-Hans.definition: 法院或仲裁庭审理和裁决争议的权力。

cards.definition: Contract clause naming the law that governs the contract.
cards.example: “This contract is governed by Swiss law, excluding the CISG.”

zh-Hans.definition: 约定合同准据法的条款。

cards.definition: Contract clause naming the courts (or arbitration) where disputes must be brought.
cards.example: The stronger party insisted on its home courts in the choice-of-forum clause.

zh-Hans.definition: 约定争议须提交特定法院（或仲裁）解决的条款。

cards.definition: Rules a court uses to pick the applicable law when parties did not choose — looking at where the contract was made, performed, and the parties’ domiciles.
cards.example: With no choice-of-law clause, the court applied conflict-of-laws rules.

zh-Hans.definition: 当事人未选择法律时，法院确定准据法的规则，考虑合同订立地、履行地及当事人住所等因素。

cards.definition: Substantive law decides the rights under the contract; procedural law governs how the case is run (in arbitration, usually the law of the seat).
cards.example: Swedish substantive law with Geneva as the seat for procedure.

zh-Hans.definition: 实体法决定合同权利义务；程序法规范案件审理方式（仲裁中通常为仲裁地法）。

cards.definition: Clause saying the written contract is the whole agreement and changes must be in writing.
cards.example: The merger clause shut out the buyer’s claim of an oral side deal.

zh-Hans.definition: 约定书面合同构成全部协议、任何修改须书面作出的条款。

cards.definition: Practices established between the parties in earlier deals; binding under the CISG.
cards.example: Ten years of 60-day payment created a course of dealing.

zh-Hans.definition: 当事人在以往交易中形成的做法；在CISG下对双方有约束力。

cards.definition: A practice widely known and regularly observed in a trade; courts increasingly treat Incoterms® as one.
cards.example: The court read “CIF” as an Incoterms® trade usage even without the word Incoterms®.

zh-Hans.definition: 在某一行业广为人知并经常遵守的做法；法院越来越多地将国际贸易术语视为此类惯例。

cards.definition: U.S. domestic rule limiting evidence of oral agreements that contradict a final written contract; not applied under the CISG.
cards.example: In MCC-Marble, the CISG let the buyer prove an oral understanding despite the parol evidence rule.

zh-Hans.definition: 美国国内法规则，限制以口头协议否定最终书面合同的证据；CISG下不适用。

cards.definition: A breach that substantially deprives the other party of what it was entitled to expect; allows termination (avoidance).
cards.example: Unusable custom tooling delivered after the season was a fundamental breach.

zh-Hans.definition: 实质上剥夺对方根据合同有权期待利益的违约；对方可宣告合同无效。

cards.definition: Most obligations performed with only minor shortfalls; the remedy is usually a price reduction, not termination.
cards.example: Shipping 9,950 of 10,000 units was substantial performance.

zh-Hans.definition: 大部分义务已履行、仅有轻微不足；救济通常为减价而非解除合同。

cards.definition: CISG term for ending the contract after a fundamental breach, releasing remaining obligations.
cards.example: The buyer declared the contract avoided after repeated non-delivery.

zh-Hans.definition: CISG术语，指在根本违约后解除合同，免除剩余义务。

cards.definition: Court order compelling a party to perform (deliver, pay, replace) rather than pay damages; less available in common law.
cards.example: Common-law courts rarely order specific performance when damages suffice.

zh-Hans.definition: 法院命令当事人实际履行义务（交货、付款、更换）而非赔偿损失；普通法系中较少适用。

cards.definition: Foreseeable knock-on losses caused by a breach, such as lost profits from an idle production line; often excluded by contract.
cards.example: The exporter’s terms excluded consequential damages.

zh-Hans.definition: 违约引起的可预见的连带损失，如生产线停工造成的利润损失；合同中常予排除。

cards.definition: Duty of the injured party to take reasonable steps to limit its loss.
cards.example: The buyer had to resell the off-spec produce instead of letting it rot.

zh-Hans.definition: 受损方应采取合理措施减少损失的义务。

cards.definition: Damages fixed in advance in the contract, e.g. a percentage per week of delay; may be unenforceable if punitive.
cards.example: 0.5% of price per week late, capped at 5%.

zh-Hans.definition: 合同预先约定的赔偿金额，如每延迟一周按价格一定比例计算；若具惩罚性可能不被执行。

cards.definition: Giving up a right, expressly or by conduct — e.g. repeatedly accepting late deliveries without objection.
cards.example: Object in writing each time so tolerance is not read as waiver.

zh-Hans.definition: 明示或通过行为放弃权利，如多次接受迟延交货而不提异议。

cards.definition: Preliminary document recording intent to contract; may become binding if detailed and without a clear disclaimer.
cards.example: The LOI helped the buyer obtain its loan approval.

zh-Hans.definition: 记录缔约意向的初步文件；若内容详尽且无明确免责声明，可能产生约束力。

cards.definition: Preliminary agreement setting out agreed points while others are negotiated; binding effect depends on wording and law.
cards.example: An MOU fixed price and volume while the parties negotiated warranty terms.

zh-Hans.definition: 在其他事项仍在谈判时记录已达成要点的初步协议；约束力取决于措辞和适用法律。

cards.definition: Standard legal terms (law, warranties, liability, disputes) that sit behind the deal-specific form, often on the reverse of a PO or pro forma.
cards.example: Our pro forma refers to our general conditions of sale printed overleaf.

zh-Hans.definition: 位于具体交易单据之后的标准法律条款（准据法、保证、责任、争议），常印于订单或形式发票背面。

cards.definition: The fill-in part of a two-part model contract: parties, goods, price, Incoterm, payment, dates for this deal.
cards.example: Leaving the payment box blank in the specific conditions triggered the default rule.

zh-Hans.definition: 两部分示范合同中需填写的部分：本次交易的当事人、货物、价格、贸易术语、付款和日期。

cards.definition: Published template (e.g. ICC model international sale contract) used as is, as a drafting source, or as a neutral negotiating benchmark.
cards.example: We pointed to the ICC model’s liability clause to rebalance the buyer’s draft.

zh-Hans.definition: 已出版的合同范本（如国际商会国际销售示范合同），可直接使用、作为起草参考或中立谈判基准。

cards.definition: Sector form contract that market participants are expected to use, e.g. GAFTA for grain, FIDIC for engineering works.
cards.example: Grain traders sign GAFTA contracts almost by default.

zh-Hans.definition: 行业参与者通常须使用的格式合同，如谷物业的GAFTA合同、工程业的FIDIC合同。

cards.definition: International Federation of Consulting Engineers — publishes standard contracts for construction and engineering projects (e.g. the Red Book).
cards.example: The power-plant tender used FIDIC conditions.

zh-Hans.term: 国际咨询工程师联合会
zh-Hans.definition: 发布建筑和工程项目标准合同（如“红皮书”）的国际组织。

cards.definition: Grain and Feed Trade Association — publishes the standard contracts used for much of world trade in grain, feed, and oilseeds.
cards.example: The wheat sale was on GAFTA terms with GAFTA arbitration.

zh-Hans.definition: 发布全球谷物、饲料和油籽贸易所用标准合同的行业协会。

cards.definition: Contract clause identifying the goods; buyers want precision, sellers only the precision they can deliver. Drives conformity and L/C wording.
cards.example: “Broiler chickens 1.5–2 kg”, not just “chicken”.

zh-Hans.definition: 确定货物的合同条款；买方希望精确，卖方只希望写明能保证交付的规格；决定货物相符性和信用证措辞。

cards.definition: Clause keeping ownership with the seller until full payment, so unpaid goods can be reclaimed if the buyer is insolvent; enforceability depends on national law.
cards.example: The RoT clause let the exporter recover unsold stock from the bankrupt distributor.

zh-Hans.definition: 约定货款付清前所有权仍归卖方的条款，买方破产时可取回未付款货物；效力取决于各国法律。

cards.definition: RoT that also claims resale proceeds, mixed or processed goods, or other debts; often unenforceable.
cards.example: The extended RoT over resale proceeds failed under local insolvency law.

zh-Hans.definition: 同时主张转售价款、混合或加工产品或其他债务的所有权保留条款；常不被认可。

cards.definition: Clause excusing performance hindered by unforeseeable events beyond a party’s control (war, disaster, strikes); often allows termination after a long suspension.
cards.example: A seven-month port strike let either party terminate under the force majeure clause.

zh-Hans.definition: 对因不可预见且无法控制的事件（战争、灾害、罢工）导致不能履行予以免责的条款；长期中止时常可解除合同。

cards.definition: Clause requiring renegotiation (or allowing adjustment) when events make performance excessively onerous though not impossible.
cards.example: Energy prices tripled, triggering the hardship clause.

zh-Hans.definition: 当事件使履行负担过重（但并非不可能）时，要求重新谈判或调整合同的条款。

cards.definition: Deadline after which a party loses the right to bring a claim.
cards.example: The model contract’s default time-bar is four years from arrival of the goods.

zh-Hans.definition: 超过后当事人丧失提出索赔权利的期限。

cards.definition: Firm date after which the buyer may cancel immediately if goods are not delivered.
cards.example: Seasonal goods carried a cancellation date of 1 November.

zh-Hans.definition: 若届时仍未交货，买方可立即取消合同的确定日期。

cards.definition: Inspection of goods before shipment, ideally by an independent agency; a strong quality and anti-fraud control.
cards.example: The buyer required PSI by an independent agency before the credit would pay.

zh-Hans.definition: 货物装运前的检验，最好由独立机构进行；是有效的质量和防欺诈控制手段。

cards.definition: Clause adjusting price over time, e.g. pegging it to a published index after an initial fixed period.
cards.example: Price fixed for six months, then indexed to the published steel price.

zh-Hans.definition: 随时间调整价格的条款，如固定期后与公布的指数挂钩。

cards.definition: Seller promises the buyer it will never pay more than any other customer; check competition law.
cards.example: The distributor negotiated a most-favoured customer clause.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方承诺买方所付价格不高于其他任何客户；需审查竞争法风险。

cards.definition: Resolving a dispute in public state courts; generally the slowest, costliest, and most confrontational option across borders.
cards.example: Litigation abroad meant local counsel, translations, and three years of hearings.

zh-Hans.definition: 通过国家法院解决争议；在跨境情形下通常最慢、最贵、对抗性最强。

cards.definition: Private binding dispute resolution by arbitrators chosen under the parties’ agreement; awards are final and enforceable abroad under the New York Convention.
cards.example: The contract sends all disputes to ICC arbitration seated in Singapore.

zh-Hans.definition: 依当事人协议由仲裁员作出有约束力裁决的私人争议解决方式；裁决终局，并可依《纽约公约》在外国执行。

cards.definition: Alternative dispute resolution — mediation, conciliation, expert opinion, mini-trial; usually non-binding and amicable.
cards.example: A tiered clause requires ADR before anyone may arbitrate.

zh-Hans.definition: 调解、和解、专家意见、模拟审判等方式；通常不具约束力且以友好协商为主。

cards.definition: Neutral third party helps the parties reach their own settlement; non-binding, and either side may walk away.
cards.example: Mediation settled the warranty dispute in two days.

zh-Hans.definition: 中立第三方协助当事人自行达成和解；不具约束力，任何一方均可退出。

cards.definition: Choosing (or racing to) the court most favourable to you, sometimes with counter-suits in other countries; prevented by a forum clause.
cards.example: With no forum clause, both sides went forum shopping.

zh-Hans.definition: 选择或抢先起诉对自己最有利的法院，有时在他国提起反诉；可通过法院选择条款避免。

cards.definition: Court procedure recognising a foreign judgment so it can be enforced locally.
cards.example: The exporter sought exequatur in the buyer’s country where the assets were.

zh-Hans.term: 外国判决承认与执行程序
zh-Hans.definition: 法院承认外国判决以便在本国执行的程序。

cards.definition: Principle that a court enforces another country’s judgments only if that country enforces its own.
cards.example: With no treaty, recognition depended on reciprocity.

zh-Hans.definition: 只有在对方国家承认本国判决时，法院才承认该国判决的原则。

cards.definition: 1958 UN convention on recognising and enforcing foreign arbitral awards; adopted by 170+ states — why awards travel better than judgments.
cards.example: The award was enforced in Brazil under the New York Convention.

zh-Hans.definition: 1958年《承认及执行外国仲裁裁决公约》，170多个国家加入，使仲裁裁决比法院判决更易跨境执行。

cards.definition: Court order preventing a defendant from moving assets until the case is decided.
cards.example: A freezing injunction stopped the buyer emptying its bank account.

zh-Hans.definition: 在案件判决前禁止被告转移资产的法院命令。

cards.definition: Judgment given against a party that fails to appear or defend.
cards.example: Ignoring the foreign lawsuit led to a default judgment.

zh-Hans.definition: 对未出庭或未答辩一方作出的判决。

cards.definition: Clause letting a long-term contract flex — price escalation, specification updates, substitution, time extensions — instead of breaking.
cards.example: The adaptation clause indexed prices to inflation after year one.

zh-Hans.definition: 使长期合同能灵活调整（价格调整、规格更新、替代、延期）而不致破裂的条款。

cards.definition: Dispute clause requiring steps in order — negotiation, then mediation, then arbitration.
cards.example: Under the tiered clause, executives must meet before mediation starts.

zh-Hans.definition: 要求按顺序进行协商、调解、仲裁等步骤的争议解决条款。

cards.definition: Independent expert assesses a technical, financial, or legal question; usually non-binding but persuasive if made close to events.
cards.example: An expert report on the turbine failure framed the later arbitration.

zh-Hans.definition: 由独立专家就技术、财务或法律问题出具意见；通常无约束力，但临近事发时作出则很有说服力。

cards.definition: Arbitration run by the parties and tribunal without an administering institution.
cards.example: Ad hoc arbitration is cheaper only if both sides cooperate.

zh-Hans.definition: 不经仲裁机构管理、由当事人和仲裁庭自行组织的仲裁。

cards.definition: Arbitration administered by an institution (e.g. ICC) under its rules, with case management and oversight.
cards.example: ICC institutional arbitration includes scrutiny of the draft award.

zh-Hans.definition: 由仲裁机构（如国际商会）依其规则管理并监督的仲裁。

cards.definition: ICC’s administrative body that supervises arbitrations, appoints and confirms arbitrators, fixes costs, and scrutinises awards — it does not decide cases.
cards.example: The ICC Court confirmed the parties’ nominated arbitrators.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会的仲裁管理机构，负责监督仲裁、指定和确认仲裁员、确定费用和核阅裁决，但不审理案件。

cards.definition: The arbitrator or arbitrators (usually one or three) who hear and decide the dispute.
cards.example: A three-member arbitral tribunal heard the case in London.

zh-Hans.definition: 审理并裁决争议的仲裁员（通常为一名或三名）。

cards.definition: The legal place of the arbitration; fixes procedural law and which courts can review the award.
cards.example: Singapore was the seat, though hearings took place in Hong Kong.

zh-Hans.definition: 仲裁的法律所在地，决定程序法及可审查裁决的法院。

cards.definition: Claimant’s filing that starts an ICC arbitration, identifying the parties and the claim, with a filing fee.
cards.example: The seller filed its Request for Arbitration with the ICC Secretariat.

zh-Hans.definition: 申请人提交以启动国际商会仲裁的文件，列明当事人和请求，并缴纳立案费。

cards.definition: ICC document summarising the case and issues, prepared by the tribunal with the parties early in the proceedings.
cards.example: Drafting the Terms of Reference showed the parties they mostly agreed.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会仲裁中由仲裁庭与当事人早期拟定的、概述案件和争议焦点的文件。

cards.definition: Deposit for arbitrators’ fees and ICC expenses, normally split 50/50; if one side does not pay, the other may pay it to keep the case going.
cards.example: The respondent refused its half, so the claimant funded the whole advance on costs.

zh-Hans.definition: 用于支付仲裁员报酬和国际商会费用的预付款，通常双方各付一半；一方不付时另一方可代付以继续仲裁。

cards.definition: The tribunal’s binding decision; normally final with no appeal on the merits.
cards.example: The award ordered the buyer to pay the price plus costs.

zh-Hans.definition: 仲裁庭作出的有约束力的决定；通常为终局，不能就实体问题上诉。

cards.definition: A settlement recorded as an arbitral award, making it enforceable like an award.
cards.example: After settling, the parties asked the tribunal for an award by consent.

zh-Hans.definition: 以仲裁裁决形式记录的和解协议，可像裁决一样执行。

cards.definition: Temporary arbitrator who can order urgent interim measures before the tribunal is constituted.
cards.example: An emergency arbitrator froze the resale of the disputed cargo.

zh-Hans.definition: 在仲裁庭组成前可下令采取紧急临时措施的临时仲裁员。

cards.definition: Adding a third party to an existing arbitration.
cards.example: The seller requested joinder of the carrier.

zh-Hans.definition: 将第三方加入已开始的仲裁程序。

cards.definition: Merging related arbitrations into one proceeding.
cards.example: Two arbitrations over the same plant were consolidated.

zh-Hans.definition: 将相关的多个仲裁合并为一个程序。

cards.definition: Fast-track arbitration with shortened steps and deadlines; ICC applies it automatically to smaller claims unless the parties opt out.
cards.example: The small claim went through the expedited procedure with a sole arbitrator.

zh-Hans.definition: 缩短步骤和期限的快速仲裁；国际商会对较小争议自动适用，除非当事人选择排除。

cards.definition: ICC document-based expert procedure for disputes under UCP, URC, URR, and URDG; non-binding unless agreed, typically 6–12 weeks.
cards.example: The banks took their discrepancy dispute to DOCDEX.

zh-Hans.term: 跟单票据争议专家解决机制
zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会针对UCP、URC、URR和URDG项下争议的书面专家程序；除非约定否则无约束力，通常6至12周。

cards.definition: Standing panel of one or three members who follow a long project and resolve disputes as they arise (DRB, DAB, or combined).
cards.example: The pipeline contract set up a dispute board at signing.

zh-Hans.definition: 由一至三名成员组成、跟进长期项目并及时解决争议的常设机构（包括DRB、DAB或组合型）。

cards.definition: Dispute board issuing recommendations that bind only if no party objects within the set period.
cards.example: The contractor objected, so the DRB recommendation did not bind.

zh-Hans.definition: 发布建议的争议委员会；仅在规定期限内无人异议时才具约束力。

cards.definition: Dispute board issuing decisions that must be complied with on receipt, even if a party objects and later arbitrates.
cards.example: The employer paid under the DAB decision while pursuing arbitration.

zh-Hans.definition: 发布决定的争议委员会；决定收到即须遵守，即使一方异议并随后提起仲裁。

cards.definition: ADR technique where a panel of a neutral plus one executive from each side gives an opinion.
cards.example: A mini-trial let both CEOs hear the strongest version of each case.

zh-Hans.definition: 由一名中立人员和双方各一名高管组成小组发表意见的替代性争议解决方式。

cards.definition: Buyer pays before shipment; no risk for the seller, high risk for the buyer. Often partial (e.g. 30%).
cards.example: 30% payment in advance, balance against documents.

zh-Hans.definition: 买方在装运前付款；卖方无风险，买方风险高，常为部分预付（如30%）。

cards.definition: Seller ships and invoices; buyer pays later (net 30/60/90). Riskiest for the seller, best for the buyer.
cards.example: Long-standing customers buy on open account, net 60.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方先发货开票，买方日后付款（30/60/90天）；对卖方风险最大，对买方最有利。

cards.definition: Credit term: full invoice amount due 30, 60, or 90 days after invoice.
cards.example: Our standard export terms are net 30 from invoice date.

zh-Hans.definition: 信用期限：发票全额须在开票后30、60或90天内支付。

cards.definition: Seller’s bank sends shipping documents and a draft to the buyer’s bank, which releases them only against payment (D/P) or acceptance (D/A). Banks take no payment risk.
cards.example: A documentary collection is the usual compromise between open account and an L/C.

zh-Hans.definition: 卖方银行将货运单据和汇票寄交买方银行，后者仅在付款（D/P）或承兑（D/A）后放单；银行不承担付款风险。

cards.definition: Collection of a draft alone, without shipping documents — effectively open account through a bank.
cards.example: Service fees were collected by clean collection.

zh-Hans.definition: 仅托收汇票、不附货运单据，实质上是通过银行进行的赊销。

cards.definition: Collection where the buyer must pay the draft to receive the bill of lading; also “cash against documents”.
cards.example: Under D/P, the buyer cannot take the goods until it pays.

zh-Hans.definition: 买方须付清汇票才能取得提单的托收方式，又称“凭单付现”。

cards.definition: Collection where the buyer accepts a time draft (promise to pay later) to receive the bill of lading now.
cards.example: Under D/A, the buyer took the goods and paid 90 days later.

zh-Hans.definition: 买方承兑远期汇票（承诺日后付款）即可取得提单的托收方式。

cards.definition: The exporter’s bank that sends the collection documents to the buyer’s country.
cards.example: The remitting bank forwarded the documents to Lagos.

zh-Hans.definition: 将托收单据寄往买方所在国的出口商银行。

cards.definition: Bank in the buyer’s country that presents the collection documents to the buyer and collects payment or acceptance.
cards.example: The presenting bank released the B/L once the buyer paid.

zh-Hans.definition: 在买方所在国向买方提示托收单据并收取货款或承兑的银行。

cards.definition: Exporter’s precise instructions to the banks (D/P or D/A, fees, protest, contacts) that travel with the documents.
cards.example: A vague collection instruction left the bank unsure whether to release documents.

zh-Hans.definition: 出口商给银行的详细指示（D/P或D/A、费用、拒付证书、联系人），随单据一同传递。

cards.definition: ICC Uniform Rules for Collections — standard banking practice for documentary and clean collections.
cards.example: The collection instruction states “subject to URC 522”.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会《托收统一规则》，规范跟单托收和光票托收的银行惯例。

cards.definition: Bank undertaking used as security: drawn only if the applicant fails to pay or perform. Usually under ISP98 or URDG.
cards.example: Open account backed by a standby L/C can be as safe as advance payment.

zh-Hans.definition: 作为担保的银行承诺，仅在申请人未付款或未履约时才被支取；通常适用ISP98或URDG。

cards.definition: Bank promise to pay on a compliant demand, independent of the underlying contract; e.g. advance-payment or performance guarantee.
cards.example: The importer’s advance payment was protected by a demand guarantee from the exporter’s bank.

zh-Hans.definition: 银行凭相符索赔付款的承诺，独立于基础合同，如预付款保函或履约保函。

cards.definition: Insurance against non-payment by foreign buyers (commercial and political risk), often from a government export credit agency.
cards.example: With credit insurance in place, the exporter offered net 60 terms.

zh-Hans.definition: 承保外国买方不付款（商业及政治风险）的保险，常由政府出口信用机构提供。

cards.definition: Selling or assigning receivables to a factor, which advances cash, manages credit, and collects from buyers.
cards.example: The exporter used factoring to get cash on its open-account invoices.

zh-Hans.definition: 将应收账款出售或转让给保理商，由其提供融资、管理信用并向买方收款。

cards.definition: Buying accepted or avalised term bills or deferred-payment claims at a discount without recourse to the exporter.
cards.example: The forfaiter paid the exporter now for the bank-guaranteed 180-day bills.

zh-Hans.definition: 以无追索权方式折价买断已承兑或保付的远期票据或延期付款债权。

cards.definition: Negotiable unconditional written order by the drawer to the drawee to pay a fixed sum on demand or at a set date.
cards.example: The exporter drew a 90-day bill of exchange on the buyer.

zh-Hans.definition: 出票人签发的、无条件要求付款人于见票时或指定日期支付一定金额的可流通书面命令。

cards.definition: Drawer = who issues the bill (usually the exporter); drawee = who is ordered to pay (the importer or a bank).
cards.example: Under the L/C the issuing bank is the drawee of the draft.

zh-Hans.definition: 出票人为签发汇票者（通常为出口商）；付款人为被要求付款者（进口商或银行）。

cards.definition: Bill of exchange payable on presentation.
cards.example: D/P collections usually use a sight draft.

zh-Hans.definition: 见票即付的汇票。

cards.definition: Bill of exchange payable at a future date, e.g. 90 days after sight.
cards.example: D/A collections use a usance draft that the buyer accepts.

zh-Hans.definition: 在未来日期（如见票后90天）付款的汇票。

cards.definition: Time draft accepted by a bank, which then owes payment at maturity; can be discounted for cash.
cards.example: The exporter discounted the banker’s acceptance to get paid early.

zh-Hans.definition: 经银行承兑、由银行到期付款的远期汇票；可贴现变现。

cards.definition: Time draft accepted by the buyer itself rather than a bank.
cards.example: A trade acceptance is only as good as the buyer’s credit.

zh-Hans.definition: 由买方本身（而非银行）承兑的远期汇票。

cards.definition: Bill of exchange with the transport document attached, so the buyer gets no rights to the goods until it pays or accepts.
cards.example: Documentary bills swap goods for money through the banks.

zh-Hans.definition: 附有运输单据的汇票，买方须付款或承兑后才能取得货物权利。

cards.definition: Third party who acquires a negotiable instrument in good faith for value and can enforce it free of many defences.
cards.example: The discounting bank became a holder in due course of the accepted draft.

zh-Hans.definition: 善意并支付对价取得可流通票据、可免受多数抗辩而行使权利的第三人。

cards.definition: A bank’s guarantee written on a bill of exchange, adding its credit to the drawee’s.
cards.example: The importer’s bank avalised the bills so the forfaiter would buy them.

zh-Hans.definition: 银行在汇票上加具的担保，以其信用补强付款人信用。

cards.definition: Selling a future payment claim (e.g. an accepted draft) for cash now, less interest and fees.
cards.example: The exporter discounted the 120-day acceptance at its bank.

zh-Hans.definition: 将未来收款权（如已承兑汇票）扣除利息和费用后提前变现。

cards.definition: Evidence of cover for one shipment under an open cover policy; must match the type of insurance document the L/C requests.
cards.example: The credit asked for an insurance policy, so the certificate was a discrepancy.

zh-Hans.definition: 在预约保单下单批货物的保险证明；须与信用证要求的保险单据类型一致。

cards.definition: Insurance contract covering all shipments over a period, with a certificate issued for each one.
cards.example: Regular exporters use open cover rather than a policy per shipment.

zh-Hans.definition: 承保一定期间内所有货运的保险合同，每批货物另出具保险凭证。

cards.definition: FX risk that the rate moves between agreeing a foreign-currency price and receiving payment; hedgeable.
cards.example: A EUR 1M sale paid in 90 days carries transaction risk for a U.S. exporter.

zh-Hans.definition: 在约定外币价格至收到货款期间汇率变动的风险；可通过对冲规避。

cards.definition: Balance-sheet FX risk from restating foreign-currency assets and liabilities in the reporting currency each period.
cards.example: The euro warehouse lost dollar value at year-end because of translation risk.

zh-Hans.definition: 每期将外币资产负债折算为报告货币时产生的资产负债表汇率风险。

cards.definition: Long-term effect of currency trends on competitiveness in a market; not removed by invoicing currency or simple hedges.
cards.example: A strong dollar for years cut the exporter’s European sales — economic risk.

zh-Hans.definition: 汇率长期走势对市场竞争力的影响；无法通过计价货币或简单对冲消除。

cards.definition: Agreement with a bank to exchange currencies at a fixed rate on a future date, removing transaction risk.
cards.example: The forward locked EUR 1M into about USD 991,000.

zh-Hans.definition: 与银行约定在未来日期按固定汇率兑换货币的合约，以消除交易风险。

cards.definition: Right but not obligation to exchange currency at a set rate, for a premium; protects downside while keeping upside.
cards.example: An option let the exporter benefit if the euro rose.

zh-Hans.definition: 支付期权费后，有权但无义务按约定汇率兑换货币；可防范不利变动并保留有利收益。

cards.definition: Bank’s irrevocable undertaking to pay the seller against documents that comply with the credit’s terms.
cards.example: The buyer’s bank issued a documentary credit for USD 250,000.

zh-Hans.definition: 银行凭与信用证条款相符的单据向卖方付款的不可撤销承诺。

cards.definition: ICC Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (2007): the rules banks apply to L/Cs when incorporated into the credit.
cards.example: Credits say “subject to UCP 600” to incorporate the rules.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会《跟单信用证统一惯例》（2007年），在信用证中引用时银行据以处理信用证业务。

cards.definition: The party entitled to draw under a credit — normally the exporter.
cards.example: The beneficiary’s name on the invoice must match the credit.

zh-Hans.definition: 有权在信用证项下支款的一方，通常为出口商。

cards.definition: The party that asks its bank to issue a credit and must reimburse it — normally the importer (also “opener” or “account party”).
cards.example: The applicant must make sure the credit matches the sale contract.

zh-Hans.definition: 要求银行开立信用证并负责偿付的一方，通常为进口商。

cards.definition: Bank that issues the credit and irrevocably undertakes to honour a complying presentation.
cards.example: The issuing bank in Jakarta debited the importer’s account.

zh-Hans.definition: 开立信用证并不可撤销地承诺对相符交单付款的银行。

cards.definition: Bank that passes the credit to the beneficiary, checking apparent authenticity; takes no payment obligation unless it confirms.
cards.example: The advising bank only relayed the credit — it did not confirm it.

zh-Hans.definition: 将信用证通知受益人并核验表面真实性的银行；除非保兑，否则不承担付款义务。

cards.definition: Bank that adds its own irrevocable undertaking to the issuer’s and pays without recourse to the beneficiary.
cards.example: A confirming bank in Germany removed the exporter’s country risk.

zh-Hans.definition: 在开证行承诺之外加具自身不可撤销承诺、对受益人无追索地付款的银行。

cards.definition: Bank authorised in the credit to honour or negotiate; not obliged to unless it has confirmed.
cards.example: The credit was available with any bank, so every bank was a nominated bank.

zh-Hans.definition: 信用证中被授权付款或议付的银行；除非已保兑，否则无付款义务。

cards.definition: Bank that advances funds to the beneficiary against complying documents before the issuer pays, usually with recourse.
cards.example: The negotiating bank advanced cash against the usance draft.

zh-Hans.definition: 在开证行付款前凭相符单据向受益人垫付款项的银行，通常有追索权。

cards.definition: Whether a bank that paid the beneficiary can claw the money back if the issuer does not reimburse: negotiating banks usually with, confirming banks without.
cards.example: Because the payment was without recourse, the exporter kept the funds.

zh-Hans.definition: 付款银行在开证行不偿付时能否向受益人追回款项：议付行通常有追索权，保兑行无追索权。

cards.definition: Credit that cannot be amended or cancelled without all parties’ consent; UCP 600 credits are irrevocable by default.
cards.example: An irrevocable credit lets the exporter start production with confidence.

zh-Hans.definition: 未经各方同意不得修改或撤销的信用证；UCP 600下的信用证默认不可撤销。

cards.definition: Credit to which a second bank (usually in the exporter’s country) has added its own undertaking.
cards.example: The exporter insisted on a confirmed credit for the new market.

zh-Hans.definition: 由第二家银行（通常在出口国）加具保兑承诺的信用证。

cards.definition: Credit payable immediately on a complying presentation.
cards.example: Under a sight credit the exporter is paid within days of presenting.

zh-Hans.definition: 相符交单后立即付款的信用证。

cards.definition: Credit payable at a future date (deferred payment or acceptance), giving the buyer time to resell.
cards.example: A 120-day usance credit let the importer sell the goods before paying.

zh-Hans.definition: 在未来日期付款（延期付款或承兑）的信用证，使买方有时间转售货物。

cards.definition: Credit for a maximum sum that renews automatically at intervals, for regular shipments.
cards.example: A revolving credit covered USD 100,000 of shipments every month.

zh-Hans.definition: 金额用完后按期自动恢复、用于定期发货的信用证。

cards.definition: Credit allowing pre-shipment advances to the beneficiary at the applicant’s risk.
cards.example: A red clause credit funded the exporter’s raw-material purchase.

zh-Hans.definition: 允许受益人在装运前预支款项、风险由申请人承担的信用证。

cards.definition: Credit the first beneficiary (a middleman) can transfer in whole or part to a second beneficiary (the supplier); must be requested by the applicant.
cards.example: The trading house transferred the credit to its factory supplier.

zh-Hans.definition: 第一受益人（中间商）可将其全部或部分转让给第二受益人（供应商）的信用证；须由申请人申请开立。

cards.definition: Second, separate credit issued for a supplier using the middleman’s incoming credit as security; the middleman owes its bank even if the first credit never pays.
cards.example: The middleman used a back-to-back credit to keep its supplier hidden.

zh-Hans.definition: 中间商以收到的信用证为担保，另向供应商开立的独立信用证；即使原证未付款，中间商仍须偿付银行。

cards.definition: Any way the presented documents fail to comply with the credit; a single one lets the bank refuse payment.
cards.example: A wrong beneficiary address was a discrepancy.

zh-Hans.definition: 提交单据与信用证条款不相符之处；任一不符点均可使银行拒付。

cards.definition: Presentation that matches the credit’s terms, the UCP, and international standard banking practice.
cards.example: A complying presentation obliges the issuing bank to pay.

zh-Hans.definition: 与信用证条款、UCP及国际标准银行实务相符的交单。

cards.definition: Doctrine that documents must match the credit precisely; “almost the same” is not enough.
cards.example: Under strict compliance, “Model 4512” vs “Model 4521” is fatal.

zh-Hans.definition: 单据必须与信用证严格一致的原则，“基本相同”并不足够。

cards.definition: A credit is separate from the sale contract: banks pay against complying documents regardless of disputes about the goods.
cards.example: The buyer’s quality complaint could not stop payment under the credit.

zh-Hans.definition: 信用证独立于买卖合同；只要单据相符，银行即须付款，不受货物争议影响。

cards.definition: Narrow exception to independence: clear evidence of beneficiary fraud can justify refusing payment; mere suspicion cannot.
cards.example: Forged bills of lading triggered the fraud exception.

zh-Hans.definition: 独立性原则的狭窄例外：有受益人欺诈的明确证据时可拒付，仅有怀疑则不可。

cards.definition: Applicant’s agreement to accept discrepant documents; sought via the issuing bank. Likely in rising markets, unlikely in falling ones.
cards.example: The buyer waived the discrepancy because it needed the goods urgently.

zh-Hans.definition: 申请人同意接受不符单据，须经开证行征询；市场上涨时较可能，下跌时不太可能。

cards.definition: Formal change to a credit issued through the banks; agreeing a change with the buyer alone does not alter the credit.
cards.example: The extended shipment date only counted once the amendment was advised.

zh-Hans.definition: 经银行正式发出的信用证变更；仅与买方协商一致并不能改变信用证。

cards.definition: Condition in a credit not linked to any required document; banks disregard it.
cards.example: “Goods must be first-class quality” with no certificate is a non-documentary condition.

zh-Hans.definition: 信用证中未要求以任何单据证明的条件；银行对此不予理会。

cards.definition: ICC International Standard Banking Practice — guidance on how banks examine documents under UCP credits.
cards.example: Under ISBP, “mashine” for “machine” is not a discrepancy.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会《国际标准银行实务》，指导银行审核UCP信用证项下单据。

cards.definition: ICC supplement to the UCP for part- or all-electronic presentations; applies only if expressly incorporated.
cards.example: A credit subject only to UCP 600 does not bring in the eUCP.

zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会针对部分或全部电子交单的UCP补充规则；仅在明确引用时适用。

cards.definition: Under UCP 600, each examining bank has at most five banking days after the day of presentation to decide whether documents comply.
cards.example: Presented Monday, the bank had until the following Monday to refuse.

zh-Hans.definition: UCP 600规定，审单银行最多在交单次日起五个银行工作日内决定单据是否相符。

cards.definition: If a credit sets no period, documents must be presented within 21 calendar days after shipment and before expiry.
cards.example: B/L dated 1 March → present by 22 March.

zh-Hans.definition: 信用证未规定交单期时，须在装运后21个日历日内且不迟于到期日交单。

cards.definition: In a credit, “about” or “approximately” before an amount or quantity allows a ±10% variation.
cards.example: “About USD 100,000” allows drawings from 90,000 to 110,000.

zh-Hans.definition: 信用证中金额或数量前的“约”或“大约”允许±10%的增减。

cards.definition: International Standby Practices — ICC-endorsed rules designed specifically for standby letters of credit.
cards.example: The standby was issued subject to ISP98.

zh-Hans.definition: 专为备用信用证制定、经国际商会认可的规则。

cards.definition: ICC Uniform Rules for Demand Guarantees — rules for bank demand guarantees (and sometimes standbys).
cards.example: The performance guarantee was subject to URDG 758.

zh-Hans.term: 见索即付保函统一规则
zh-Hans.definition: 国际商会《见索即付保函统一规则》，适用于银行保函（有时也适用于备用证）。

cards.definition: Irrevocable bank-to-bank payment undertaking triggered by electronic data matching, an alternative to paper L/Cs.
cards.example: The model contract lists the BPO among available payment methods.

zh-Hans.definition: 基于电子数据匹配触发的银行间不可撤销付款承诺，是纸质信用证的替代方式。
